newsitem.title: USA: NFL-CHARGERS NAME KEVIN GILBRIDE HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: NFL-CHARGERS NAME KEVIN GILBRIDE HEAD COACH.

text.p: Kevin Gilbride, who as offensive coordinator helped the Jacksonville Jaguars advance to the AFC Championship Game in their second season, was named head coach of the San Diego Chargers on Saturday.
Gilbride succeeds Bobby Ross, who stepped down January 3 and was later named head coach of the Detroit Lions.
The 45-year-old Gilbride has been with the Jaguars each of their two NFL seasons and his unit led the NFL in passing offence and was second overall in 1996.
Gilbride is credited with developing Mark Brunell of the Jaguars into one of the better quarterbacks in the NFL.
Prior to joining the Jaguars, Gilbride was offensive coordinator of the Houston Oilers from 1990-92 and was promoted to assistant head coach/offense in 1993-94.

Despite his success, Gilbride is probably best known for his long-running feud with former Oilers' defensive coordinator Buddy Ryan and was punched by Ryan on the sidelines during a nationally-televised game.
Under Gilbride, the Oilers ranked in the top three in the NFL in total offence for four straight seasons.

A former quarterback at Southern Connecticut State, Gilbride has served as an assistant at Idaho State, Tufts and American International. He returned to Southern Connecticut State in 1980 for his only head coaching experience and was 35-14 over five seasons.
Gilbride was also an assistant with Ottawa of the Canadian Football League and at East Carolina before joining the Oilers.

Gilbride takes over a team that is just two seasons removed from its only Super Bowl appearance. The Chargers were 8-8 in 1996 and failed to make the playoffs after being eliminated in the wild card round a year before.
